title: Short-acting beta-agonists: Article 31 referral. Restrictions on use of short-acting beta-agonists in obstetric indications – CMDh endorses PRAC recommendations
authors: European Medicines Agency; Coordination Group for Mutual Recognition and Decentralised Procedures – Human
journal: European Medicines Agency, procedure EMEA/H/A-31/1347, reference EMA/565019/2013, first published 25 October 2013, with Annex II scientific conclusions
funder: European Medicines Agency and the EU national competent authorities; review initiated on 27 November 2012 at the request of the Hungarian medicines agency
result: The review covered fenoterol, hexoprenaline, isoxsuprine, ritodrine, salbutamol and terbutaline in obstetric use, with data from clinical studies, post-marketing reports and the literature; no inhaled formulation was authorised for obstetric indications. For salbutamol, 98 reports with cardiovascular events were identified, most of them arrhythmias such as tachycardia or palpitations; two reports of tachycardia were fatal; pulmonary oedema contributed to several events, one with cardiomegaly after five weeks of tablets; eight infant fatalities were noted, two with pulmonary oedema and cardiovascular events; reports involved both intravenous and oral salbutamol. PRAC concluded that oral and suppository forms of short-acting beta-agonists carry serious, dose-dependent cardiovascular risk to mother and fetus, mostly with prolonged use, with very limited efficacy data, and should no longer be used in any obstetric indication; products authorised only for obstetric use were to be revoked and recalled by 25 November 2013. Injectable forms were restricted to 48 hours between 22 and 37 weeks of gestation under specialist supervision, contraindicated with pre-existing ischaemic heart disease or significant risk factors for it, with monitoring of blood pressure, heart rate, electrocardiogram, electrolyte and fluid balance, glucose, lactate and potassium. PRAC recommendation 5 September 2013; CMDh position 23 October 2013.
